progress.text: · A ruler guide dragged with the Selection tools, out of a ruler, on its own or with other selected guides, snaps along its axis as objects do (#1221): to other ruler guides, margins, columns, bleed, page and object edges and centers (with the smart-guide mark) and the document grid, within the snap zone and following Snap to Guides and Smart Guides. Shift snaps to the ruler's ticks and Cmd suspends snapping. The preview line, the position readout and the drop use the same snapped position. No readiness percentage change.

· macOS: the app menu has a Language submenu after Settings… with each interface language in its own name and the current one checked, as in the suite's other apps; Preferences › General › Interface Language stays. No readiness percentage change.

· macOS menu bar: the menus keep working after the interface language or Show CJK Features changes (a rebuilt menu bar lost every click, Quit included), and its key equivalents are the shortcuts in effect, so a shortcut moved in the Keyboard Shortcuts editor leaves its old menu item. No readiness percentage change.

· Paragraph rules: Rule Above's offset is measured from the first line's baseline to the rule's bottom edge, as in InDesign. Rules sat one ascent too high and crossed the previous paragraph's text (reported from an imported INDD document). No readiness percentage change.

· Ruler guides are selected like objects (#1282): a click with the Selection tools selects a guide (also where it crosses an object), Shift-click adds or removes one, a new guide from the rulers is selected, a marquee that touches no object selects the guides it crosses, and Edit › Select All Guides (⌥⌘G, guide.selectAll) selects every unlocked guide on the spread. Selected guides draw thicker in their layer's color, drag together (all of them shown moving), nudge with the arrow keys and go with Delete, each as one undo step (guide.select, guide.deselect, guide.moveBy, guide.delete {}). With one guide selected the Control bar's X (vertical guide) or Y (horizontal guide) field and Properties › Transform show where it is, as the rulers measure, and typing a value moves it there. No readiness percentage change.

· View › Screen Mode: Bleed and Slug do what they say. Both were selectable from the toolbar, the View menu and view.screenMode but drew the canvas exactly as Normal did, guides and all; they are preview modes now, and what each page shows reaches the bleed box or the slug box instead of stopping at the trim. The slug guide is drawn as well, in the Slug colour from Preferences › Guides & Pasteboard, which nothing had read. No readiness percentage change.

· File › Package writes the document's and the IDML's links relative to the package (Links/logo.png, file:Links/logo.png), so a package holds no path from the machine that made it; opening a document resolves them to the files beside it. Links › Copy Link(s) To still links by full path. (#340). No readiness percentage change.
· Object strokes reject malformed types and unknown type fields before changing the document; command help lists every stroke kind and its required fields. No readiness percentage change.
· Docs: documented a persistent source CLI install with Cargo, MCP-client PATH setup and bare-name server registration in docs/mcp.md. No readiness percentage change.

· Selection: drag a column guide to move its gutter, as in InDesign (#1096). Both guides of the gutter move together and keep its width, stop at the neighbouring guides and the margins, and snap to the document grid, guides and objects, or with Shift to the ruler's tick marks; Escape cancels and the drag is one undo step. Locked column guides (the default) are not picked. A document page takes the result as its own columns; on a parent page it passes to the pages that follow it. layout.moveColumnGuide does the same over the control channel and MCP. No readiness percentage change.

· Layout: autoflow, inserted pages and new parents follow dragged column guides (#1096). Autoflow sets one frame per dragged column and counts the pages it adds from them; Insert Pages and New Parent keep the custom positions with the column count and gutter; a page that moves to the other side of the spine (inserted, deleted or moved pages, Duplicate Spread, a new parent's other page) has them mirrored across its margin box, as InDesign does; document.inspect reports each page's gutter, column rects and whether its columns are custom. No readiness percentage change.

· Layout: Margins and Columns keeps dragged column guides unless the column count or gutter changes (#1096). The dialog sends every field on OK, so a margin-only change re-divided the columns evenly. Margin changes keep the positions; the columns follow them only while they fit the margin box. No readiness percentage change.

· Lock Guides and Lock Column Guides are commands in View ▸ Grids & Guides (view.lockGuides, ⌥⌘;, and view.lockColumnGuides), so the control channel and MCP reach them. Lock Column Guides is an undo step, is saved with the document, on in new ones, and read from and written to IDML's ColumnGuideLocked, which export always wrote as locked (#1096). No readiness percentage change.

· IDML: a page keeps column guides that were dragged off centre (InDesign's Custom columns). They were divided evenly on import, so the gutter sprang back to the middle; the imported positions now place the columns, with the canvas guides, snapping and text placement following them, and they are written back on export. Layout › Margins and Columns re-divides them evenly when the count or gutter changes, as InDesign's does. No readiness percentage change.

· IDML: custom column positions are checked before they are used (#1096). A set must give two edges per column, ascending from the left margin to the right one; any other (a wrong count, unsorted or non-numeric values, a list longer than 216 columns allow, or positions left behind by a margin or page-size change) is the even split, in the canvas, on import and on export, instead of columns drawn outside the margins. No readiness percentage change.

· Type › Reload Fonts (font.reload): fonts installed, edited or removed while DesignCraft runs are read again without a restart, and the open documents recompose with them (#328, #547). An edited font file is noticed by its length and modification time; bundled, added and document fonts stay as they are. InDesign does this by itself, so noticing changes automatically is still open (gap 6). No readiness percentage change.

· Parents can be deleted from their Pages-panel context menu or layout.parents.delete {id}. Applied-page and based-on references are cleared, local override copies survive, and Undo restores the parent. Addresses the deletion portion of #956; no readiness percentage change.

Lock Column Guides is an undo step, is saved with the document, on in new ones, and read from and written to IDML's ColumnGuideLocked, which export always wrote as locked (#1096). · Threading: the loaded text cursor threads into a text frame inside a group (it hit the group and showed it could not thread); a plain click still selects the group (#1075). Gap 27 closed. No readiness percentage change.

· Greek text hyphenates. The patterns were never compiled in, so Greek set unhyphenated however narrow the column; "Greek", "Greek: Greece", el and el-GR all resolve now and ανθρωπος breaks αν-θρω-πος. They are the monotonic patterns (hyph-el-monoton, Dimitrios Filippou, under MIT), which is what polytonic text hyphenates by too. Five of InDesign's ~40 hyphenation languages. No readiness percentage change.

· A swatch applied to a placed greyscale or bitmap image colours it, as in InDesign: IDML's <Image FillColor> is read and written, greyscale pixels become a tint of the swatch on opaque white and a bitmap's white lets the frame show through, on screen and in PDF (spot swatches print on their plate). Colour images keep their colours. Applying the swatch from the Swatches panel comes next. No readiness percentage change.

· Color Theme: the toolbar tool previews up to five colours from a placed raster and adds them as one undoable swatch group. Local deterministic extraction; transparent padding is ignored. No readiness percentage change.
· Applying text styles removes matching local formatting so capture sources
· Redefine paragraph and character styles from local formatting, including the
· Paragraph Styles marks local character overrides and offers Clear Overrides
· Existing paragraph and character styles preview their attribute edits in
· Paragraph Style Options summarizes captured and pending color, size and
· Typography uses named panel groups with the Control panel and restores that

· Character panel: dragging a variable font axis slider previews on the page and is one undo step when let go (with several axes it piled up an undo step per frame); each axis takes a typed value, and narrow axes (Skia's 0.48–3.2) step by hundredths instead of jumping to whole numbers. The fields line up in two columns, auto leading shows in parentheses, and an axis-set style shows its axes. New edit.preview / edit.commitPreview / edit.cancelPreview commands give panels, the control channel and MCP live previews. No readiness percentage change.

· Selection tool: once a frame's content is selected (double-click, or the content grabber), the pointer is a hand over it and a drag anywhere on it moves the content inside the frame (Shift keeps one axis), as in InDesign; it moved the frame unless the press was on the grabber. No readiness percentage change.

· Scaling a text frame (Cmd+Shift-dragging a handle, the Scale tool, Transform panel scale fields) sets its text larger or smaller and leaves the frame at 100%, as InDesign's default When Scaling: Apply to Content does; it used to keep the text's size with the scale on the frame. No readiness percentage change.

· With nothing selected, the Tools panel's fill and stroke (the Color Picker, swatches, Apply None, Swap, Default) set the colours new shapes are drawn with, as InDesign's document defaults; the proxy shows them. They were refused ("nothing selected").

· The Eyedropper with text selected picks up the formatting of the text it clicks (character style and overrides, paragraph style and overrides) and applies it to the selection, as InDesign's does; it copied the clicked frame's fill and stroke instead. No readiness percentage change.
